faq.q: How much property transfer tax does a first-time buyer in BC actually save?
faq.a: A qualifying buyer is exempt from PTT on the first $500,000 of the purchase price, provided the property's fair market value is $835,000 or less, it is 0.5 hectares or smaller, contains only residential improvements and is used only as the buyer's principal residence; above $835,000 and under $860,000 only a partial exemption applies.

faq.q: What are the general PTT rates the calculator starts from?
faq.a: 1% of fair market value up to and including $200,000, 2% on the portion over $200,000 up to and including $2,000,000, and 3% on the portion over $2,000,000 — plus a further 2% on the residential portion over $3,000,000 where that applies.

faq.q: Is a newly built home treated differently from a resale home?
faq.a: Yes. The newly built home exemption has a full-exemption threshold of $1,100,000 with a phase-out to $1,150,000, and a new home may also attract GST, which the federal first-time home buyers' GST/HST rebate can offset by up to $50,000 for eligible buyers.
